title: Motie van het lid Beckerman over een bevoegde instantie aanwijzen om ook deepfakeporno en andere onrechtmatige seksuele beelden offline te halen

reading.body:
AI-generated deepfake pornography was deployed at scale on a platform accessible to millions of people without any technical check to prevent impersonation or sexual abuse. The system created fake videos of real people by their faces without consent, enabling the creation of revenge porn of politicians, athletes, entertainers, and other public figures. This is impersonation through synthetic media, used to harm and humiliate identifiable individuals.

The failure was almost entirely in deployment rather than the model itself. The platform hosted the material and profited from views without implementing age verification, consent checks, identity verification of subjects, or any filter to detect synthetic sexual content. A prior case showed that prosecution is possible when reports are filed, but only after harm occurs and only if the perpetrator can be identified.

Whether the platform knew deepfakes were being created and uploaded, or failed to detect them despite reasonable technical means available, is not established by these reports.

summary:
Multiple well-known Dutch women are considering legal action after appearing in manipulated pornographic videos on an online platform that receives 13 million visitors monthly. The platform hosts numerous fake videos featuring Dutch artists, television presenters, Olympic athletes, government officials, mayors, and members of the royal family. Justice Minister Yesilgöz called the videos disgusting and urged victims to file reports. Managers and representatives of various victims confirmed to the news service that they have filed complaints or are considering legal action.

Deepfake pornography falls under revenge porn laws and is therefore criminal. Users who upload material are advised to remain anonymous to avoid prosecution, and they earn more money when videos receive more views. Legal experts recommend victims file reports, which allows prosecutors to attempt shutting down the website. Other options include starting a class action lawsuit, filing complaints with data protection authorities, or contacting hosting companies. Previously, TV presenter Welmoed Sijtsma pursued legal action against a 39-year-old man from Amersfoort who created deepfake videos of her, resulting in his conditional sentence of 180 hours in November.
title_en: Motion by member Beckerman on designating a competent authority to also remove deepfake pornography and other unlawful sexual images offline
